Order denying (741) Motion for Leave to Appeal in case 3:23-cv-03417-VC: The motion for leave to file an interlocutory appeal is denied. To be sure, the issue presented in the motion is a difficult one, and Judge Alsup's opinion makes a good point. But it won't be long before a final judgment is entered in at least one of the Meta cases before this Court. That judgment will allow the issue presented in the current motion, along with many other important issues relating to the use of copyrighted materials in the training of AI models, to be presented to the Court of Appeals as part of a tidy package. coverage.headline: AI vs. Authors Update: Court Approves Historic Anthropic Settlement While Meta Litigation Continues
coverage.summary: With the Bartz v. Anthropic class action receiving final approval of its $1.5 billion settlement on July 20, 2026, the article contrasts that resolution with the ongoing Kadrey v. Meta case, which remains active through further pleading and discovery. Disputed privilege claims over internal Meta communications about torrenting and uploading copyrighted material have been resolved by a magistrate judge in Meta's favor.

coverage.headline: AI in Litigation Series: An Update on AI Copyright Cases in 2026
coverage.summary: Norton Rose Fulbright's litigation update notes that while the court granted partial summary judgment for Meta on fair use grounds regarding LLM training, claims related to reproduction of pirated works during 'seeding' in the torrenting process remain active in the Northern District of California. The piece situates Kadrey among six landmark AI copyright cases reshaping copyright law.

coverage.headline: AI Infringement Case Updates: June 18, 2026
coverage.summary: The Kadrey plaintiffs moved to certify summary judgment issues for interlocutory appeal to the Ninth Circuit, arguing that whether acquisition-by-piracy can be excused by an ultimately fair use is an unresolved question and that resolving the divergence between the Kadrey and Bartz rulings is needed. The case's active contributory and distribution claims continue on the existing schedule.

coverage.headline: AI Infringement Case Updates: May 5, 2026 — Discovery Extended, Deposition Cutoff Set for August 15
coverage.summary: Judge Chhabria granted in part plaintiffs' request for a discovery extension in Kadrey v. Meta, setting a new fact discovery cutoff of July 1, 2026 and a deposition cutoff of August 15, 2026 — deadlines that govern the live contributory infringement and distribution claims. The extension reflects the complexity of the torrenting-focused discovery phase.

coverage.headline: AI Infringement Case Updates: April 7, 2026
coverage.summary: Notes that plaintiffs filed their Fourth Amended Complaint adding contributory-infringement claims after the court 'reluctantly' granted leave, and reports that the first amicus briefs in support of plaintiffs—including from the RIAA—were filed in the related proceedings.

coverage.headline: Judge Allows BitTorrent Seeding Claims Against Meta, Despite Lawyers' 'Lame Excuses'
coverage.summary: Judge Vince Chhabria granted plaintiffs' motion for leave to amend to add a contributory infringement claim based on Meta's alleged BitTorrent seeding, while sharply criticizing plaintiffs' counsel for failing to include the claim in the November 2024 amendment. The court found Meta would not be meaningfully prejudiced, allowing the claim to proceed.

coverage.headline: Meta Argues BitTorrent Seeding Is Fair Use in AI Training
coverage.summary: Reports that Meta's discovery responses in Kadrey v. Meta assert that downloading books via BitTorrent for AI training still qualifies as fair use, even as the case continues on the remaining distribution and contributory-infringement theories.

coverage.headline: AI Infringement Case Updates: February 24, 2026 — Plaintiffs Say 'No Harm, No Foul' Despite Inexcusable Delay
coverage.summary: Kadrey plaintiffs filed supplemental briefing arguing their late motion to add contributory infringement and uploading-based claims should be permitted because Meta faced no prejudice and delay was not in bad faith, even after Judge Chhabria called the delay 'inexcusable.' Entrepreneur Media, newly added as a plaintiff, separately flagged that the existing discovery cutoff was ill-suited to the torrenting-focused discovery both it and Kadrey plaintiffs need.

coverage.headline: AI Infringement Case Updates: February 16, 2026 — Judge Denies Stay, Calls Amendment Delay 'Inexcusable'
coverage.summary: Judge Chhabria denied Meta's request to stay the Kadrey case pending discovery in Entrepreneur Media and provided tentative views at a hearing, including a finding that plaintiffs' delay in amending to add contributory infringement claims was 'inexcusable.' Meta argued this finding alone warranted denial of the amendment motion, with additional briefing ordered from both sides.

coverage.headline: AI Infringement Case Updates: January 19, 2026 — Meta Opposes Amendment, Seeks Stay
coverage.summary: Meta formally opposed the Kadrey plaintiffs' December 2025 motion to add contributory copyright infringement claims based on seeding of torrented materials, arguing the amendment is futile and was inspired by the parallel Entrepreneur Media case. Meta simultaneously sought a stay of Kadrey pending coordinated discovery in Entrepreneur Media to promote judicial efficiency.
